landmarks.name: Vasa Museum
landmarks.writeup: A maritime museum in Stockholm displaying the 17th-century warship Vasa, which sank on its maiden voyage.

wiki.extract: The Vasa Museum is a maritime museum in Stockholm, Sweden. Located on the island of Djurgården, the museum displays the only almost fully intact 17th-century ship that has ever been salvaged, the 64-gun warship Vasa that sank on her maiden voyage in 1628. The Vasa Museum opened in 1990. Together with other museums such as the Stockholm Maritime Museum, it belongs to the Swedish National Maritime-, Transport-, and Military Museums.

landmarks.name: Gamla Stan
landmarks.writeup: The old town of Stockholm, known for its medieval alleyways, cobbled streets, and historic architecture.

wiki.extract: Gamla Stan, until 1980 officially Staden mellan broarna, is the old town of Stockholm, Sweden. Gamla Stan consists primarily of the island Stadsholmen. Gamla Stan includes the surrounding islets Riddarholmen, Helgeandsholmen and Strömsborg. It has a population of approximately 3,000.

landmarks.name: Drottningholm Palace
landmarks.writeup: The private residence of the Swedish royal family, a UNESCO World Heritage site with beautiful gardens.

wiki.extract: Drottningholm Palace, or Drottningholm, one of Sweden's royal palaces, situated near Sweden's capital Stockholm, is the private residence of the Swedish royal family.

landmarks.name: Icehotel
landmarks.writeup: A unique hotel in Jukkasjärvi made entirely of ice and snow, rebuilt annually.

wiki.extract: The Icehotel is a hotel in northern Sweden, about 17 kilometers from Kiruna. It is rebuilt each year with snow and ice in the village of Jukkasjärvi and is the world's first ice hotel.

landmarks.name: Abisko National Park
landmarks.writeup: A national park in Lapland known for its natural beauty and as a prime location to view the Northern Lights.

wiki.extract: Abisko National Park is a National Park in Sweden, established in 1909.

cultural_events.name: Midsummer
cultural_events.writeup: A major Swedish celebration marking the summer solstice with dancing, singing, and traditional foods.

wiki.extract: Midsummer or Midsommar is a celebration of the season of summer, taking place on or near the date of the summer solstice in the Northern Hemisphere, the longest day of the year. The name midsummer mainly refers to summer solstice festivals of European origin. These cultures traditionally regard it as the middle of summer, with the season beginning on May Day. Although the summer solstice falls on 20, 21 or 22 June in the Northern Hemisphere, it was traditionally reckoned to fall on 23–24 June in much of Europe. These dates were Christianized as Saint John's Eve and Saint John's Day. It is usually celebrated with outdoor gatherings that include bonfires, maypole dancing and feasting.

cultural_events.name: Walpurgis Night
cultural_events.writeup: A spring festival celebrated with bonfires and singing to welcome the arrival of spring.

wiki.extract: Walpurgis Night, an abbreviation of Saint Walpurgis Night, also known as Saint Walpurga's Eve and Walpurgisnacht, is the eve of the Christian feast day of Saint Walpurga, an 8th-century abbess in Francia, and is celebrated on the night of 30 April and the day of 1 May. This feast commemorates the canonization of Saint Walpurga and the movement of her relics to Eichstätt, both of which occurred on 1 May 870.

cultural_events.name: Lucia Day
cultural_events.writeup: A festival of light celebrated on December 13th, featuring processions and singing to honor Saint Lucia.

wiki.extract: Saint Lucy's Day, also called the Feast of Saint Lucy, is a Christian feast day observed on 13 December. The observance commemorates Lucia of Syracuse, an early-fourth-century virgin martyr under the Diocletianic Persecution. According to legend, she brought food and aid to persecuted Christians hiding in the Roman catacombs, wearing a candle-lit wreath on her head to light her way, leaving both hands free to carry as much food as possible. Because her name means "light" and her feast day had at one time coincided with the shortest day of the year prior to calendar reforms, it is now widely celebrated as a festival of light.

food_writeup: Swedish cuisine features dishes like meatballs, pickled herring, crispbread, and lingonberry jam, emphasizing fresh, local ingredients and traditional preservation methods.
brief_history: Sweden has a history dating back to the Viking Age, evolving into a unified kingdom in the 12th century. It became a major European power in the 17th century and has maintained neutrality in conflicts since the early 19th century, developing a strong welfare state and democratic governance.

important_people.name: Alfred Nobel
important_people.description: Inventor and founder of the Nobel Prize

current_conflicts: Sweden is not involved in any active military conflicts but participates in international peacekeeping and diplomatic efforts.
